steps.text: Place ground beef and onion in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook, stirring to crumble, until beef is browned; drain.
Transfer the beef and onion to a slow cooker and stir in ketchup, sugar, vinegar, and mustard. Season with Worcestershire, salt, celery seed, and pepper.
Cover and simmer on Low for 3 hours before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Grandpa's Classic Coney Sauce
raw_recipe.description: Coney sauce is ground beef simmered with tangy flavors that gets served on hot dogs with chopped onion. A tasty, nostalgic recipe for any occasion.

video.description: This chili sauce is the best way to top a hot dog!
video.name: How to Make Grandpa's Classic Coney Sauce

review.reviewBody: This is CONEY sauce. Not chili! Ten stars! just upped the ketchup a bit.also try adding dry minced onion instead of fresh. gives it bolder onion flavor.i also reduced vinegar.if you put meat in food processor it makes it more of a classic coney consistency. then to make the flavor really cook together well, i slow cooked in the crock pot.

Excellent coney sauce. This not a chili dog recipe. There is a difference between a coney and a chili dog. If you want a chili dog, search for a chili dog recipe. I used one of those hand blenders (boat motors) to get the meat fine after I added the sauce.

This was so good that my husband couldn't stop and ate 4 coneys! He said it was a little sweet, but really good. My son thought it was really good but different from the chili type sauce he is used to. Both of them have said they want this again. I thought this was almost like sweet tomatoey sloppy joes. I did add water to the beef in the skillet before I cooked it so it would break into fine pieces instead of being chunky when it browned. Thanks for posting this Sean, your Grandpa's sauce is a hit!

Fantastic CONEY SAUCE ! Please don't give this recipe a bad review because it isn't chili sauce - read the title first, the word "chili" does not appear in it. Being a kid of the late 50's and 60's, this is absolutely like the Coney Sauce that we loved on the footlongs from our little Mom and Pop diner/drive-in. Make sure you slow cook this for hours either in the crock pot or at low heat on the stove top or tightly coverd in a 250 degree oven. I cut the sugar to a tablespoon and a half since I used honey mustard. Thanks for a trip down Memory Lane!

DELICIOUS! I scaled the recipe back to use onlt 3/4 pound of meat b/c that's all I had and that was plenty for us. After cooking/draining the meat and onion mixture, I finely ground it in my food processor. I then proceeded w/ the recipe, only allowing it to simmer on the stove instead of the slow cooker, until I felt it was done. I would like to try it in the slow cooker sometime, I just didn't have time. I think while this did rival sloppy joe to an extent, it was just different enough, and we LOVED it on our hot dogs! NOTE: I actually made this last week when I had to use the meat and froze it until I needed it...worked perfectly! I will def make this again~YUM! Thanks for sharing. :)

Thanks for this recipe and feedbacks below. My second trial: indeed, this easy to prepare sauce with simple ingredients is sweet enough with the ketchup. Gone the sugar. Celery seed is essential. Yes to the immersion blender at mid cooking in the skillet (under a wax paper to control splashes) … did adjust the consistency with more water considering it should be a soupy beef sauce and that I did all in the skillet. Did grill a top split hot dog bun with the dog in and added the sauce, cheese and mustard after. Miam!

thank goodness I didn't add vinegar, there is more than plenty from the ketchup! I will add ground vs prepared mustard next time as well. not the most authentic coney sauce, but then I live in Michigan and know what the real deal tastes like. this is edible, but far from true coney sauce. to the unitiated, it might be ok. a tip from me, add 1/4-1/2 c water per pound of lean ground beef, and double the onion, super fine dice, and definitely add some garlic....not just powder, while cooking the beef. it makes the beef fall apart to the proper consistency without blenders and the garlic helps to balance all that added vinegar from the prepared mustard and ketchup. then cook the out of it. I agree with another reviewer that there is just something off. after tasting, I also added some other spices to combat the shock of vinegar. So as not to make it too sweet, I used 1/2 the called for sugar. this recipe is an easy cheat, but so off from true coney sauce, never mind not using beef heart, which is hard for most of us to source. the search for a real coney sauce continues!!! nice try grandpa! I gave 3 vs just 2 stars, because it is easy peasy and made with readily available pantry items, and is passable for the folks who have never had true coney sauce.

I don’t brown the hamburger just throw everything together and let it simmer til the hamburger is cooked. Then pulse it with an immersion blender to get the perfect consistency. Put it in the crockpot on low for a couple hours. Let cool then package in freezer bags for a quick supper!!! Super easy supper when you’re in a hurry!

Here's what is needed to turn this into coney sauce and not sloppy joe mix. First of all the hamburger needs to be very finely chopped and then add a can of refried beans to the meat mixture in the slow cooker and mix it together well then cook. Then it is delicious and true coney sauce. You're welcome. :) Oh I will also add if you use ketchup don't add sugar if you add sugar, you should use crushed canned tomatoes. I used ketchup with the sugar thought it was just a tad too sweet. But I will be honest. With the refried beans, this recipe was delicious.

Pretty darn good. Easy to make, I use frozen ground beef, add water & "steam" cook the ground beef breaking up the beef with a potatoe masher. I can get the cooked ground beef to that smooshed up consistency. Tranfer to a slow cooker, add the rest of the ingrediants. It is a tad sweet, but if you think of it as a condiment, it's perfect. IT IS NOT anything like a chili but by the time you add raw onions, relish, mustard, whatever your favorite add ons to the hot dog- delicious! Will make again, a little less sweet for my personal taste.

My wife made it. She is an excellent cook by reputation and used just one tablespoon of sugar. It was off the chart good. Per one of the other reviews put the hamburger in the food processor after you fry it and grind it up. Wow! Can’t say enough good things about this recipe. Don’t forget to use a high end hot dog.
This coney sauce recipe is delicious! Will be using it from now on
Great coney sauce recipe as-is, not to be confused with chili sauce. It's reminiscent of old rootbeer stand days! Top with a little finely shredded sharp cheddar & diced onion - great for gamedays!
Made it as directed. Fantastic! Already2 requests for the recipe. I wouldn't change a thing (other than maybe a little cayenne or hot sauce for those who like a kick). No more sauerkraut for mr!
Sweet
Finally a Perfect Coney Sauce! Yum
Superior!
Its not a bad recipe but like other reviews mentioned you definitely need to reduce or completely remove the sugar. Way too sweet
Delicious. I recommend making the day before. Flavors were better after being in the fridge overnight.

I added a little cumin and a little dark chili powder ( I know chili isn’t coney or NJ but lol omg) thank you very much also I browned the meat in tomato sauce before draining it may sound crazy but trust me💯. It would sell all day in a restaurant
